relations.subject: Sheng-yen
relations.evidence: Ven. Sheng-yen, who had been an active writer in the Humanity Magazine under his pen-name Xing Shi Jiang Jun ("World Awakening General"), became Ven. Dongchu's disciple in 1959.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: At his early education period, he studied with various prominent monks such as Master Aiting and Master Nanting from the Zhulin Buddhist Institute in Zhenjiang.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: He then pursued his study further at Minnan Buddhist Institute in Xiamen, and studied under renowned scholar-monk and modernist Master Taixu.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: After graduating from Minnan Buddhist Institute, Ven. Dongchu then became dean of the prestigious school Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: At the same time, he was abbot of the Dinghui Monastery in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu province.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: He also taught classes at several other Buddhist institutes, including Jingan Si (Quiet Calm) Academy in Shanghai

relations.subject: Sheng-yen
relations.evidence: Jingan Si (Quiet Calm) Academy in Shanghai – at which young Sheng-yen, who was studying there, first encountered him.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: Three months later, his passion for Buddhist education and culture led him to start the Humanity Magazine – the first Buddhist periodical in Taiwan.

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: Ven. Dongchu established his first monastery in Taiwan at 1955. It was located in Beitou, near Taipei, and was completed a year later. Instead of naming it a 'monastery', he named it Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Culture

relations.subject: Dongchu
relations.evidence: Step by step, he built a farmhouse, and after four years of works, he succeeded to establish another monastery, Nung Chan Monastery in 1975.
